topic: The service catalog that generates an invoice automatically when a case is closed — what that does for cash flow
format: Build a sharp before/after: managing government services with WhatsApp and Excel versus SmartPRO Hub case tracking and a client portal — show the same week, completely different experience
post:
Monday, 8 AM. Your WhatsApp has 74 unread messages.

Three clients asking for status updates on work permits. Two asking if their visa renewals are done. One upset because they didn't know an MOL filing was pending — and now there's a fine.

You open Excel. You scroll. You try to remember which tab has Al Zahrani Trading's files.

Now picture the same Monday — different office.

Cases opened, tracked, and closed inside one system. Every client sees their own portal. No one calls to ask "what's the status?" because they already know.

And when a work permit case closes? The invoice generates automatically. No chasing. No end-of-week invoicing pile. Cash hits your account faster because the billing is built into the workflow.

That's what a service catalog tied to your case management actually does for a Sanad office.

It's not a feature. It's the difference between collecting payment 30 days late and collecting it the same week the work is done.

For offices managing 20+ client companies — that gap in cash flow is real money sitting idle every month.

How many closed cases from last month are still waiting on an invoice?
